title: General deductions — s 8-1 ITAA 1997
summary: Facet map: is a loss/outgoing deductible under s 8-1? Spine: positive limbs (s 8-1(1)(a) incidental-and-relevant nexus — Ronpibon Tin; s 8-1(1)(b) necessarily incurred in business — FCT v Day) → negative limbs (s 8-1(2)(a) capital — Sun Newspapers enduring benefit; (b) private/domestic; (c) exempt/NANE related; (d) statutory bar via s 12-5 list) → specific deductions (s 8-5) and no double deductions (s 8-10). FACETS: apportionment ('to the extent that'), incurred timing (James Flood), employee work expenses (TR 2020/1, TR 1998/9), repairs vs improvements (s 25-10), specific denial provisions (Div 32 entertainment, s 26-5 penalties, s 26-20 bribes, s 26-30 uniforms). Subsection coverage: s 8-1(1)-(3) on the spine; s 8-5(1)-(3), s 8-10 mapped; s 12-5 and the denial provisions mapped to the denials facet.

nodes.label: You have incurred a loss or outgoing — is it deductible under s 8-1?
nodes.body: Single question, many facets. Spine: positive limbs → negative limbs → specific deductions. Facets on the side branches carry the niche issues and where-to-look signposts.

nodes.label: Positive limb (a): incurred in gaining or producing your assessable income?
nodes.body: The nexus test: the loss must be 'incidental and relevant' to the process of gaining or producing assessable income (Ronpibon Tin NL v FCT (1949) 78 CLR 47). The expense need not actually produce income — it must be incurred in the course of the income-producing activity. Note the 'to the extent that' apportionment language.

nodes.label: Or limb (b): necessarily incurred in carrying on a business for that purpose?
nodes.body: Available only where a business is carried on. 'Necessarily incurred' means clearly appropriate and adapted for the purpose, not absolutely essential (FCT v Day (2008) 236 CLR 163). Wider scope than limb (a) for business expenses generally.

nodes.label: Not deductible under s 8-1 — no nexus
nodes.body: Fails both positive limbs. Check for a specific deduction provision (s 8-5) before concluding.

nodes.label: Negative limb (a): is it capital or of a capital nature?
nodes.body: The enduring-benefit test (Sun Newspapers Ltd v FCT (1938)): expenditure for acquiring an asset or advantage of enduring benefit is capital. Repairs, running costs and consumables are revenue. Trading losses on revenue account are NOT excluded merely because they are 'losses'.

nodes.label: Not deductible — capital (s 8-1(2)(a))
nodes.body: Capital outgoings are excluded. Look to specific capital allowances: Div 40 depreciation, Div 43 capital works, s 40-880 business related costs (blackhole expenditure).

nodes.label: Negative limb (b): private or domestic nature?
nodes.body: Excludes private/domestic outgoings . Apportionment: the private portion of a mixed outgoing is not deductible. 'Inherently private' expenses (ordinary clothing, food, home-to-work travel) are excluded; the income-producing portion of e.g. a home office may be deductible if separately identifiable.

nodes.label: Not deductible — private/domestic (s 8-1(2)(b))
nodes.body: Denied only to the extent of the private/domestic portion — apportion before concluding. Separately identifiable income-producing portions remain deductible.

nodes.label: Negative limb (c): incurred in relation to exempt or NANE income?
nodes.body: Expenses of deriving exempt income or NANE income are not deductible. Apportionment applies. NANE examples: foreign branch income (s 23AH), NANE foreign dividends (s 768-5).

nodes.label: Not deductible — exempt/NANE related (s 8-1(2)(c))
nodes.body: Denied only to the extent the outgoing relates to exempt or NANE income — apportion before concluding. Apportion where the outgoing relates partly to assessable income.

nodes.label: Negative limb (d): does a provision prevent the deduction?
nodes.body: Specific denial/limitation provisions. See s 12-5 for the summary list: entertainment (Div 32), penalties (s 26-5), bribes to foreign public officials (s 26-52), non-compulsory uniforms (s 26-30), and others. Note: Div 35 — non-commercial business losses (see s 8-1(1) Note) may prevent losses from non-commercial business activities being offset.

statute.title: Summary list of provisions about deductions

nodes.label: Not deductible — denied/limited by specific provision (s 8-1(2)(d))
nodes.body: Denied or limited (e.g. Div 32 entertainment, s 26-5 penalties). Check the specific provision for its own exceptions.

nodes.label: Is it a specific deduction under s 8-5 (or denied by s 8-10 no-double-deduction)?
nodes.body: s 8-5: amounts deductible under provisions outside Div 8 are 'specific deductions'. If the amount is within a specific deduction provision, it is deductible as a specific deduction; s 8-10 prevents double deduction if s 8-1 would also apply.

nodes.label: Deductible as a general deduction (s 8-1)
nodes.body: Deductible to the extent it satisfies s 8-1(1) and is not excluded by s 8-1(2). Recoupment watch: insurance/indemnity recoupment may be assessable (Subdiv 20-A). GST: Div 27 adjusts deductions for input tax credits. s 8-1(3): General deduction defined; GST adjustment (Div 27); recoupment (Subdiv 20-A).

nodes.label: FACET — Apportionment ('to the extent that')
nodes.body: Where to look: s 8-1(1) 'to the extent that'; Ronpibon Tin (1949) — apportionment where the outgoing serves both income and non-income purposes; s 8-1(2) also apportions between assessable and exempt purposes. Cases: Ronpibon Tin NL v FCT (1949) 78 CLR 47, FCT v Day (2008) 236 CLR 163.

cases.note: Ronpibon Tin NL v FCT (1949) 78 CLR 47 — incidental and relevant test; apportionment

nodes.label: FACET — 'Incurred': timing and quantum
nodes.body: Where to look: CCH 'when-is-a-loss-or-outgoing-incurred'. A loss/outgoing is incurred when the taxpayer has a presently existing liability (even if not yet paid) — James Flood Pty Ltd v FCT (1953). Contingent liabilities are not incurred until the contingency resolves. Provisions for estimated expenses are generally not deductible (unless specific provision).

nodes.label: FACET — Employee work expenses
nodes.body: Where to look: TR 2020/1 (employees: deductions for work expenses under s 8-1); TR 1998/9 (self-education); TD 1999/62 (work-related expenses). Employee expenses must have a sufficient connection to earning employment income and be substantiated; home-to-work travel is private.

rulings.title: employees: deductions for work expenses under section 8-1

nodes.label: FACET — Repairs vs improvements (revenue vs capital)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 25-10 (repairs) and the capital boundary; CCH 'revenue-vs-capital-outgoings-and-losses'. Repairing an asset to its original state is revenue; improving or replacing the asset (putting it in a better state) is capital. The 'restoration vs improvement' line (Lurcott v Wakely, FCT v Western Suburbs Cinemas).

nodes.label: FACET — Specific denial provisions (s 12-5 list)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 12-5 summary; Div 32 entertainment (limited deduction), s 26-5 penalties, s 26-52 bribes to foreign public officials, s 26-30 non-compulsory uniforms, s 26-35 leisure facility expenses, s 26-45 expenses of a strike, s 26-50(1) travel expenses where accompanied by spouse, s 26-54 political donations, s 26-55 recreational club expenses, s 26-60 (no deduction for certain legal expenses of a capital nature).

nodes.label: Deductible as a specific deduction under s 8-5 (not under s 8-1)
nodes.body: The amount is deductible under a provision outside Division 8 (s 8-5). s 8-10 prevents double deduction if s 8-1 would also apply.

No — not a specific deduction (or apply s 8-10)
Yes — deductible under a specific provision
